habitat: Usually in pairs in bushveld and woodland, often in bird parties. It feeds among branches and trunks.
summary: A common resident. It looks tailless, is grey above, and is a variable burnt orange below. It has a distinct eyebrow and a dusky eye-stripe. The song is a loud 'tree-cheer', and the call is a short dry trill. The Kemp name Longbilled Crombec and the code RB were left unchanged.

bill.shape: More prominent than the Red-faced Crombec.

head.pattern: A distinct eyebrow, a dusky eye-stripe, and paler feathering about the face and ear coverts.

tail.shape: So short that the bird looks tailless.

viewNotes.note: Grey above, with an eyebrow, a dusky eye-stripe and an almost absent tail.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: A loud urgent 'tree-cheer, tree-cheer, tree-cheer'. The call is a short dry trill. The grade A song is from Hoedspruit. The filename is XC368190-170405_Long-billedCrombec_Blydepoort_OC.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Burnt orange is not a colour name, so no underpart colour is stored. The grade A song is from Hoedspruit, and the filename says Blydepoort. The Kemp name Longbilled Crombec and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^18=262144 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 131072–524288.
